claims.text: Large Language Models are prone to hallucinations where the model generates incorrect information.
Data noise, incompleteness, and bias affect the frequency of hallucinations in LLM architectures.
Improving data quality decreases the occurrence of LLM hallucinations.
Improving data quality enhances LLM reliability for practical applications in domains such as healthcare, finance, and law.

evidence.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown surprising efficacy in natural language understanding and generation, but they are prone to hallucinations-where the model writes things that are simply wrong.
Empirical evaluation examined how various levels of data noise, incompleteness and bias affect the frequency of hallucinations in state-of-the-art LLM architectures.
Results show that by improving the data quality we are able to decrease the occurrence of hallucinations.
Results show that improving data quality improves the reliability of the LLMs for practical application in various areas including healthcare, finance, and law.

methodologies.name: Empirical evaluation of data quality factors
methodologies.description: Empirical evaluation measuring the impact of varying levels of data noise, incompleteness, and bias on hallucination rates across LLM architectures.

limitations.text: Large Language Models are prone to hallucinations and generating factually wrong statements.

future_work.text: Implementation of improved dataset construction, data augmentation, and Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) to increase model factuality.
